item.title: Solved: How to Understand and Fix Strict Aliasing Rule Violations in C and C++
item.description:
“Solved: How to Understand and Fix Strict Aliasing Rule Violations in C and C++”

When working with C or C++, encountering “strict aliasing” violations can lead to subtle bugs and unpredictable program behavior. This crucial rule is designed to enable aggressive compiler optimizations, but improper pointer usage can inadvertently trigger undefined behavior, making your code unreliable. This deep dive clarifies what strict aliasing entails, why it matters, and practical strategies to resolve common violations.

item.title: C++ Null Pointer Member Function Calls: Undefined Behavior Explained
item.description:
“C++ Null Pointer Member Function Calls: Undefined Behavior Explained”

What happens when you attempt to invoke a member function of a class using a pointer that is currently nullptr in C++? This scenario directly leads to undefined behavior, a critical concept in C++ programming where the program’s execution can be unpredictable. Let’s delve into the nuances of this situation, supported by explanations from the C++ standard and practical observations.

The core issue stems from the fundamental rule that dereferencing a null pointer results in undefined behavior. When you call a member function through a null pointer, the C++ standard dictates that this action is not permissible and can lead to any outcome, from a program crash to seemingly normal execution (which is itself a form of undefined behavior).

item.title: When is using an uninitialized variable undefined behavior?
item.description:
C Undefined Behavior Unpacking Uninitialized Variables and Potential Crashes

When working with C, particularly concerning variable initialization and memory management, encountering “undefined behavior” can lead to unexpected outcomes and potential program crashes. This discussion delves into the specifics of why using uninitialized variables, especially those with automatic storage duration and whose addresses are never taken, can result in undefined behavior, and what implications this has for program execution.

One critical aspect to consider is the C standard’s definition of how uninitialized variables behave. The standard specifies that if an object with automatic storage duration is not explicitly initialized, its value is indeterminate. This “indeterminate value” is further defined as being either an unspecified value or a trap representation.
